topics.topic: Determinism requirement and enforcement for admitted functions
questions: What happens when permitted Python code produces different results for the same inputs, and how is such nondeterminism detected or refused?
What is the outcome when code obtains time or randomness through a standard-library entry point not in the frozen trap list?
Is referentially deterministic output a required invariant for every implementation, and if so how are other Python runtime observables that can vary between executions prevented or detected?
Does deterministic mean only that verdict calculation over recorded outcomes is deterministic, or must arbitrary admitted Python execute repeatably on equal inputs?

quotes:
The list is closed for the release; an
   entry point found missing is added by a new release.
judgement.why: The determinism question concerns unchanged sandbox rules and the change did not make it matter.

topics.topic: Valid service base URLs and exact URL-joining semantics
questions: Which exact `api_base_url` forms are valid, and what exact URL results for each allowed form?

Are user information, query strings, fragments, non-root path prefixes, repeated trailing slashes, IPv6 zone identifiers and other valid absolute-URL components allowed, and exactly how are they joined and represented in the `Host` header?
What exact base-URL forms are valid, and how are authority, base paths, queries, fragments and trailing slashes joined?

judgement.why: The URL-joining rule is unchanged and the change did not make its open component cases matter.

topics.topic: Validity of admissions and activations across runtime releases
questions: Does an admission verdict remain valid after the sandbox runtime or dependencies change, or must the release/runtime identity participate in admission and activation?
After an upgrade changes the Python runtime or sandbox dependencies, do existing admission verdicts remain valid even though the same implementation may execute differently?
What happens to existing verdicts and activations when a new release changes Python, libraries, traps or sandbox behavior?

quotes:
A release pins the exact versions of the kernel's Python dependencies and of
   the sandbox runtime (A03);
judgement.why: Release identity in admission existed as a question before the change and was not affected by it.

topics.topic: Atomicity and crash recovery of implementation admission and activation
questions: After a crash partway through admission, which of the Implementation, TrialExecutions, AdmissionVerdict and Activation may exist, and how does resubmission continue?
Must writing the admitted verdict and its automatic activation be one atomic store transaction, and what state is recovered if the process stops between them?

quotes:
An `admitted` verdict is followed at once, in the same request, by an
   Activation M09 by the kernel — unless that implementation already is the
   current activation, in which case nothing is recorded.
judgement.why: The admission-to-activation durability passage is unchanged and the change did not alter its crash boundary.

topics.topic: Canonical and first-failure ordering of equal-key edges and constants
questions: How are two edges with the same endpoints but different guards ordered for first-failure reporting and canonical identity?
How are multiple constants targeting the same port ordered before the proof rejects them and before the flow version is hashed?
What total tie-break order is used so reordered equal-key edges/constants have one identity and one deterministic first failure?

quotes:
edges, by (`to_node`, `to_port`, `from_node`, `from_port`): both ports exist
      with the right direction;
judgement.why: The incomplete tie-break key was present unchanged before reopening and the change did not make it matter.

topics.topic: Classification and ordering of manifest validation failures
questions: How are wrong-typed fields, malformed capability entries, unknown fields, and oversized manifest structures classified and ordered during proposal, acceptance and send checks?

How are wrong JSON types, duplicate object member names, malformed capability entries, and malformed instance or required-header containers classified and ordered when the listed fields exist but do not have the assumed shapes?

judgement.why: Manifest field types, container schemas, unknown-field policy and structural format validation belong to State 6.

topics.topic: Distinguishing resource-limit termination from an unrelated sandbox crash
questions: How does the kernel distinguish an abnormal exit caused by an enforced memory or process limit from an unrelated crash when both conditions appear true?
What exact observable conditions count as each resource limit being hit, and when does the same symptom instead become `crashed`?

quotes:
a limit hit (memory, process count,
   scratch, `output_bytes`) — `resource_exhausted`; a trap of rule 4 raised —
   `sandbox_violation`; the module failed to load, has no `run`, raised, or the
   process exited abnormally — `crashed`;
judgement.why: Recognition of resource-limit termination is governed by unchanged sandbox text and was not affected by the change.

topics.topic: Durable pinning of a run's exact flow activation
questions: How is the exact FlowActivation authority for a delayed or recovered draft-write send durably identified?
How can a later draft-write identify the exact activation under which the run started after other activations have been recorded?

quotes:
The run pins the flow version and, for every function node, the implementation
   of the current activation at start (M19).
judgement.why: The run-pinning passage is unchanged and the change did not create the missing flow-activation pin.

topics.topic: Effect of lowered global ceilings on existing artifacts and resubmissions
questions: What happens to existing trial fixtures, stored values, pending run spools, requests and service responses that exceed a newly lowered global ceiling not stored in a contract version?
When an old contract is resubmitted unchanged after ceilings were lowered, is it returned as an existing record or refused by current-ceiling validation?

quotes:
A new release may change ceilings. They bind contract versions issued after
   it; a contract version issued earlier keeps its bounds and executes under them
   even when they exceed the new ceilings, and recorded executions are never
   reinterpreted.
judgement.why: The effect of lowered ceilings on existing non-contract artifacts was already open in unchanged text.

topics.topic: Exact JSON request serialization and content type
questions: What exact JSON byte serialization and `Content-Type` value are used for a non-multipart request body?
What exact `Content-Type` header is sent for JSON bodies?

quotes:
for
   `POST`, `PUT` and `PATCH` they form one JSON object body keyed by port name.
judgement.why: The JSON-body serialization and content-type passage is unchanged and the reopening change did not make it matter.

topics.topic: Exact path-placeholder text conversion and percent-encoding rules
questions: Which characters remain unescaped, what hex-letter case is used, how integers are converted to text, and how an existing percent sign or Unicode string is encoded?
What exact percent-encoding is used for path values, and are empty and dot-segment results allowed?

quotes:
Placeholder values are percent-encoded so that they
   stay one segment. Nothing else is normalized.
judgement.why: The placeholder-encoding rule appears unchanged in both versions and was not affected by the change.

topics.topic: Filesystem ownership and permissions required for private data storage
questions: Which owners, file types and permission bits pass the startup privacy check for the directory, database, value area, fixtures and spool?
What exact filesystem ownership and permission conditions constitute private storage?

quotes:
The directory and everything in it
   are private to the kernel's user; the kernel refuses to start otherwise.
judgement.why: The private-storage requirement is unchanged and the change did not alter its filesystem interpretation.

topics.topic: HTTP response-header limits and limit-exceeded outcomes
questions: What limits apply while reading response metadata, and how is exceeding one classified for read and non-read operations?
What response-header limits are enforced, and which outcome applies when they are exceeded?

quotes:
The
   size counted is the response body's bytes after transfer decoding.
judgement.why: Response-metadata limits were already unspecified in unchanged transport text.
judgement.failure: the quoted passage is not found verbatim in both versions

topics.topic: Outcome when an HTTP response body fails after final headers arrive
questions: If a valid 2xx, 4xx, 5xx or 3xx status and headers arrive but the body then times out, resets or ends prematurely, does the status row decide the outcome or does the earlier “no valid final response” row win?
After a final status is received but its body is incomplete, does the status row or the no-valid-response row decide the outcome?

quotes: The outcome of one attempt is decided in this order:
judgement.why: The ambiguity between incomplete bodies and status-based rows predates the change and its ordering passage is unchanged.

topics.topic: Persistence of list-level disclosure class for many-file values
questions: Where is the disclosure class of a many-file list stored, especially for an empty list that has no SpooledFile record from which a class can be derived?
Where is the list-level disclosure class of a many-file reference, especially an empty list, persisted for trace reading and recovery?

quotes:
a file list is the
   elements' SpooledFiles in element order, each keeping its own record, and
   the reference naming the list carries the list's class, so an empty one
   keeps it.
judgement.why: The changed text explicitly places the list-level disclosure class on the reference, including for an empty list.

topics.topic: Preventing echoed credentials from entering failure details
questions: How does the kernel prevent a service credential echoed in an error body from being persisted as `failure_detail`?
How is the no-credential-in-failure-detail invariant enforced against echoed or reflected credentials?

quotes:
It never enters the store, a record, a trace, a preview, a
   failure detail, a log line, a process argument or a response.
judgement.why: The prohibition on credentials in failure details is unchanged and reflected-response handling was not made relevant by the change.

topics.topic: Required and permitted fields in authored trial-case inputs and expected outputs
questions: Must a trial case supply exactly every input port and no unknown ports, or may inputs be missing or extra?
When `expected_outputs` is present, must it contain exactly every output port, or may it specify only a subset?
Must authored `inputs` contain exactly every input port, and when `expected_outputs` is present must it contain exactly every output port?

quotes:
Either
   way it is added only when its input values fit the contract version's input
   ports, its expected outputs, when present, fit the output ports, and every
   value is within `stored_value_bytes_max` and every file within
   `trial_fixture_bytes_max` — the first failing condition in this order is
   named, ports taken in name order and, for one port, presence, carriage,
   schema, then size.
judgement.why: Trial-case port presence and exactness concern unchanged admission text and were not affected by the change.

topics.topic: Retry behavior for an unchanged invalid token configuration
questions: If an invalid changed configuration remains byte-for-byte unchanged, is it parsed again on every request or skipped because its hash equals the last attempted read?
After a changed file is readable but fails parsing or token validation, is its digest recorded as the “last read” digest, and how is the same unchanged file retried on later requests?

quotes:
Before evaluating each request the kernel reads the configuration file and
   compares the SHA-256 of its bytes with that of the last read;
judgement.why: The baseline used after an invalid reread was already unspecified in this unchanged clause.

topics.topic: Sandboxed function filesystem access boundaries
questions: May agent code itself read or write arbitrary paths in the exchange directory or read the runtime, or are those paths accessible only to the sandbox runner?
May agent code read runtime files and freely read or write the exchange directory, or must filesystem access be restricted to the supplied input and runner-managed output only?

quotes:
A function node runs one admitted implementation of one contract: declared input
in, declared output out, no network, no filesystem beyond its input, no clock, no
randomness, no secret, no service handle.
judgement.why: The filesystem-access boundary is unchanged and the reopening change did not make it matter.

topics.topic: Spool deduplication, reference-safe deletion, and quota accounting
questions: Are identical spooled files shared across runs or attempts, and if so how can one run's spool be deleted without affecting another run?
Are spooled bytes deduplicated across attempts or runs, and do repeated logical files count once or repeatedly toward `spool_run_bytes_max`?

quotes: Equal bytes are stored once.
judgement.why: The scope of spool deduplication and its quota accounting were already open under this unchanged clause.

topics.topic: Validation and encoding of multipart port names and media types
questions: How are quotes, backslashes, control characters, non-ASCII text and other characters in a port name escaped or refused when inserted into multipart header parameters?
Which port names and media types are valid for HTTP bindings, and how are quoted-string characters encoded in multipart headers?

quotes:
Each part has exactly two
   headers: `Content-Disposition: form-data; name="<port>"`, with
   `filename="<port>"` added for a file part, and `Content-Type`, the port's
   media type for a file part and `application/json` for a value part, without
   parameters; nothing else.
judgement.why: Multipart name and media-type validation concern unchanged request-building text.

topics.topic: Whether multipart approval covers semantic parts or exact wire bytes
questions: Does approval cover the exact multipart bytes and boundary sent on the wire, or only the abstract ordered parts?
Must the boundary and exact multipart wire bytes be stable and approval-covered, or is approval intentionally over a semantic multipart description rather than the actual request?

quotes:
The body is described as the JSON body's bytes, or for
   `multipart/form-data` as the parts in order, each as its name, filename when
   present, media type and the SHA-256 of its content, so the boundary is not
   part of it: equal parts give equal descriptions.
judgement.why: The semantic multipart approval description is unchanged and the change did not alter its relationship to wire bytes.

topics.topic: Which implementations are eligible as rollback targets
questions: Exactly which implementations are eligible for rollback?

What makes an implementation “earlier”: submission order, activation order, or merely being different from the current implementation, and may a later previously activated implementation be selected after rolling back?

quotes:
Rollback activates an earlier implementation of the slot's current contract
   version that already holds an `admitted` verdict over the current corpus; it
   runs no admission.
judgement.why: The meaning of earlier for rollback was already left open by this unchanged passage.

topics.topic: Accepted authentication-token grammar and byte representation
questions: What exact token grammar and byte representation are accepted?

topics.topic: Actor provenance for executions and recovery actions
questions: How is the actor or triggering action of each trial execution, run advancement and startup-recovery execution recorded?

topics.topic: Applicable size ceilings for service file responses
questions: Does the 1 MiB stored-value ceiling apply to a service file response, or only the spool and service-response ceilings?

topics.topic: Conversion of non-UTF-8 HTTP error bodies into failure details
questions: How is a non-UTF-8 error body converted into bounded failure detail?

topics.topic: Crash-consistent ordering between database and filesystem operations
questions: What ordering, recovery journal and failure result make publication, run-end cleanup and release crash-consistent?

topics.topic: Disclosure class of empty mapped output lists
questions: For an empty mapped function with a higher-class non-mapped input, what class do its empty output lists receive?

topics.topic: Equality semantics for guard values
questions: Is guard equality based on canonical JSON bytes, JSON structural equality, or host-language equality, particularly for numeric forms such as 1 and 1.0?

topics.topic: Global ordering of stored records and intra-transaction updates
questions: What is the exact global ordering scheme and intra-transaction order for every record type and update?

topics.topic: Historical actor identity across agent reuse or renaming
questions: Does reuse or renaming denote the same historical agent actor or a different one, and how are their records distinguished?

topics.topic: How loopback eligibility for plain HTTP is determined
questions: Is loopback determined from the literal host syntax, DNS resolution, every resolved address, or the address actually connected to, and do names such as `localhost` qualify?

topics.topic: Locating and consistently reading a manifest revision
questions: How exactly is a manifest file at a revision located and read, and what failures occur for an unknown or changing revision?

topics.topic: Ordering and precedence of global startup checks
questions: What is the fixed order of configuration, token, credential-header collision, data-directory, lock, manifest-dependent, sandbox-probe and recovery checks when several would fail, and which failure is reported first?

topics.topic: Outcome for missing or corrupt persisted request payloads
questions: What status or refusal results when persisted input bytes required to rebuild a request cannot be read or verified?

topics.topic: Pagination behavior when records newly match above a cursor
questions: What happens when a previously nonmatching record above the cursor changes status and begins matching before the next page?

topics.topic: Runtime and dependency components pinned by a release contract
questions: Which exact CPython patch version, bubblewrap version/features, OS facilities and HTTP/TLS dependencies are part of the release contract?

topics.topic: Runtime release used when recovering an existing run
questions: Does a run pin its sandbox release, or may restart recovery execute its pinned implementation under a newer runtime than the one under which the run started?

topics.topic: Serialization and bounds of outbound HTTP header values
questions: What character repertoire, byte encoding and maximum length apply to required-header and credential values?

topics.topic: Storage and disclosure of trial-execution sandbox failure details
questions: Are sandbox failure details retained for trial executions, and if so where are they stored and disclosed?

topics.topic: Stored idempotency value for malformed read-operation keys
questions: What value is stored when a read operation has a malformed, non-string or otherwise unparsable `idempotency_key` entry?

topics.topic: Trailing-byte removal rules for credentials
questions: Exactly which trailing bytes are removed before emptiness, control-character and header-value validation?

topics.topic: Validity and ordering of empty node identifiers versus flow endpoints
questions: Is an empty `node_id` invalid, or how is it ordered and distinguished from a flow endpoint?

topics.topic: When a mapped element is final rather than retryable
questions: Does “concluded element” mean any element with a NodeExecution, or only an element whose overall conclusion is final rather than a retryable wait?

topics.topic: Whether continuation tokens are forbidden in responses
questions: Does rule 7 mean only authentication and service-credential tokens, or are continuation tokens forbidden too?

topics.topic: Whether implementation defects reject creation or only fail admission
questions: Which code defects refuse creation of the Implementation itself, and which merely produce failed trial/admission evidence after it is stored?

topics.topic: Whether many-valued inputs may be path placeholders
questions: May a `many` input port be used as a path placeholder, and if so how is its list represented?
